1. J Infect Dis. 2019 Nov 6;220(12):1962-1966. doi: 10.1093/infdis/jiz410.

Dose-Dependent Infectivity of Aseptic, Purified, Cryopreserved Plasmodium 
falciparum 7G8 Sporozoites in Malaria-Naive Adults.

Laurens MB(1), Berry AA(1), Travassos MA(1), Strauss K(1), Adams M(1), Shrestha 
B(1), Li T(2), Eappen A(2), Manoj A(2), Abebe Y(2), Murshedkar T(2), Gunasekera 
A(2), Richie TL(2), Lyke KE(1), Plowe CV(3), Kennedy JK(4), Potter GE(4), Deye 
GA(5), Sim BKL(2), Hoffman SL(2).

Author information:
(1)Malaria Research Group, Center for Vaccine Development and Global Health, 
University of Maryland School of Medicine, Baltimore.
(2)Sanaria, Inc, Rockville, Maryland.
(3)Duke Global Health Institute, Duke University, Durham, North Carolina.
(4)The Emmes Corporation, Rockville, Maryland.
(5)Parasitology and International Programs Branch, Division of Microbiology and 
Infectious Diseases, National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases, 
National Institutes of Health, Bethesda, Maryland.

Direct venous inoculation of 3.2 × 103 aseptic, purified, cryopreserved, vialed 
Plasmodium falciparum (Pf) strain NF54 sporozoites, PfSPZ Challenge (NF54), has 
been used for controlled human malaria infection (CHMI) in the United States, 4 
European countries, and 6 African countries. In nonimmune adults, this results 
in 100% infection rates. We conducted a double-blind, randomized, 
dose-escalation study to assess the infectivity of the 7G8 clone of Pf (PfSPZ 
Challenge [7G8]). Results showed dose-dependent infectivity from 43% for 8 × 102 
PfSPZ to 100% for 4.8 × 103 PfSPZ. PfSPZ Challenge (7G8) will allow for more 
complete assessment by CHMI of antimalarial vaccines and drugs.
